messages:
Maria: FYI — short spike in us-west-2 GPU pool around 02:10 PDT caused queue depth to triple and we started seeing 429s from admission controller.
Ashok: Ok can you paste the admission logs + pool status?
Maria: Logs snip:
```
[02:10:21] admission: soft-admit:true queued=245 inflight=112 hard-rejects=18
[02:10:33] warmpool: available=6 target=4 scaling:requested=8 active=6
```
Also saw TCP retransmits on node-ns-12, small network blip.
Lee: Looks like a short provisioning lag + network jitter. Policy currently uses 5% warm-pool + 5m scaleDown cooldown, right?
Maria: Correct. Proposal: for regional peak windows (18:00-21:00 UTC) bump warm-pool to 12% for gptx-heavy shards, reduce scaleDown cooldown to 2m, and add a provisional circuit-breaker threshold: if queue >200 for >30s then redirect lower-tier model or return soft-429 with Retry-After.
Priya: Cost note — 12% warmpool across prod region increases reserved GPU-hours ~+9% for us-west-2. Can we do adaptive windowing instead of flat bump?
Maria: Yes — suggestion: ramp warm-pool up 15min before expected traffic using historical forecast. Also enable short-lived hedged probes to reduce tail latency: probe duplication x2 with 120ms jitter.
Ashok: Can we implement as a canary? I'd rather not global-change overnight.
Lee: I'll author a canary plan: 1) target shard-usw2-a (10% traffic) 2) apply warmpool=12% + cooldown=2m + cb=queue>200 3) monitor 30m window metrics (queue, 429s, cost). If 429 down >80% and latency stable, expand.
Priya: Add cost dashboard card and set alert if reserved GPU-hours delta >+6% in 1h.
ops-bot: Runbook link: https://wiki.redwood/sre/runbooks/warm-pool-circuit-breaker
ops-bot: Kicking off canary: /deploy canary shard-usw2-a config=warmpool-12-cb-200
Maria: Thanks — I'll keep an eye on the probe traces and network errors. Ping me if 429s persist after canary.
Lee: will post follow-up in 30m with graphs :bar_chart:
